scope: C1 COMPOSITIONAL VOICE pre-merge review: apps/life-call/lib/voice-turn.cjs, compositional-voice.cjs, compositional-live.cjs (+ their .test.js) and the server.js /ws wiring, reviewed against specs/behavioral-spec.md C1 (fresh context, disk only).

evidence.description: Confirmed by full read: Gemini Live is never opened on this path (no openGeminiLive/new WebSocket(geminiLiveWsUrl) call anywhere in server.js; grep across apps/life-call confirms the only new WebSocket(geminiLiveWsUrl(...)) call is lib/call-bridge.cjs:206 inside startServer(), which is gated by `if (require.main === module)` at call-bridge.cjs:269 and therefore dead when the service runs via `npm start` = `node server.js` (server.js only imports routeTelnyxMessage/buildTelnyxMediaFrame from call-bridge.cjs). DTMF is confirmed logged-and-ignored at server.js:436-438 (no escalation). `liveWsOpened` in server.js:383 is a plain, never-reassigned `const 0`, making Goal-1's live_ws_opened=0 invariant structurally guaranteed for every call handled by this handler.

Confirmed deleted (Glob for apps/life-call/lib/voice-cheap* = no results) and no remaining import of voice-cheap anywhere in apps/life-call (grep-confirmed). package.json's `test` script (line 9) no longer references voice-cheap.test.js and now runs lib/voice-turn.test.js, lib/compositional-voice.test.js, lib/compositional-live.test.js — matches the spec's 'npm test updated accordingly' requirement.

The multi-sentence streamed-response test and the empty-transcript (no LLM call) test are both read and correctly exercise their stated behavior in isolation. The energyVAD frame-timing question raised in the review brief was hand-verified NOT a bug: resamplePcm16 (call-logic.js:120-140) preserves audio DURATION when upsampling 8k→16k (only sample COUNT changes), so a Telnyx 20ms media frame is still a 20ms frame after resampling to 16k, and energyVAD's `needed = ceil(silenceMs/frameMs)` counts PUSH CALLS not bytes — the silenceMs math holds correctly at 16k.

pcm16ToWav header hand-verified correct (44-byte RIFF/WAVE/fmt/data header, byteRate/blockAlign formulas standard, matches compositional-live.test.js:7-15's byte-level assertions). parseGroqSSE hand-verified correct including partial-JSON tolerance. groqLlmStream's buffering (buf.lastIndexOf("\n") splits complete-vs-partial lines across chunks) is correct: only lines before the last newline are parsed each read, the remainder is preserved in buf across the next chunk — no truncation/duplication risk found.

ttsToMuLawFrames→chunkMuLawToFrames returns an array of base64 strings; server.js's send() iterates that array and calls buildTelnyxMediaFrame(state.streamSid, f) per frame, matching buildTelnyxMediaFrame's documented (string,string)->{event,media:{payload}} signature exactly — no shape mismatch.

Import surface is otherwise clean: only routeTelnyxMessage/buildTelnyxMediaFrame remain imported from call-bridge.cjs (no geminiSetupForEvent/routeGeminiMessage import, confirming the Live-specific wiring was actually removed from server.js, not just unused-but-imported).

live_ws_opened is a hardcoded const 0, logged verbatim at carrier-close (server.js:445) — the strongest possible disk-level guarantee of Goal-1's counter invariant (it cannot become nonzero without a code change), independent of any live call. This part of Goal 1 IS provable from disk alone.

findings.issue: Barge-in only sends Telnyx {"event":"clear"}; it never actually stops the outbound send LOOP as C1 explicitly requires. respond()'s per-sentence tts()+send() loop has no cancellation check against the botSpeaking flag pushCallerFrame flips false on barge-in, and server.js:435 calls convo.pushCallerFrame without awaiting it, so a new caller utterance can trigger a second, concurrent respond() while the first is still mid-flight. Net effect: audio from an interrupted answer can keep playing (or interleave with the new answer) after the caller has already barged in and Telnyx has already been told to clear.
findings.fix: See findings/FIND-201.json for the full trace + fix (per-turn cancellation token checked before every tts()/send() call; await pushCallerFrame in server.js; add a test asserting no further audio after mid-response barge-in).

findings.issue: C1's MUST fallback chain (Groq→faster-whisper-local/Deepgram for STT, Groq→Gemini-Flash-text/DeepSeek for LLM, edge-tts→Kokoro/piper for TTS) is not wired: missing GROQ_API_KEY closes the call outright instead of degrading to local providers; STT/LLM/TTS errors degrade to empty-string/canned-line/null instead of calling any fallback provider; the tested chooseSttProvider/chooseLlmProvider selectors in voice-turn.cjs are never called from production code. A total TTS failure for a turn can leave the caller in literal silence, violating C1's explicit 'Never a silent call' invariant.

C1's QUALITY BAR requires the opening line to name event + place + route + urgency, but start() passes a hardcoded {} for the route argument to buildWakeLine, and no code path (ctxFromReq, buildStreamUrl) carries route/line/duration data over the /ws wire at all — the wake line can never mention the route.

msedge-tts remains an unused dependency despite the spec explicitly instructing its removal during impl; chooseSttProvider/chooseLlmProvider are dead (tested, uncalled) code; server.js's compositional media handler redundantly runs a full Gemini-shaped PCM transcode (via routeTelnyxMessage) that is immediately discarded on every inbound frame, duplicating the real decode done one line later.

No real-call E2E evidence exists for the compositional two-way loop under review; the only E2E transcripts on disk are for the SUPERSEDED one-way edge-tts-clip design (the spec itself calls that design 'WRONG'), and the current server.js no longer contains the symbols (openGeminiLive/playWakeClip) that those transcripts were proving out.
